title: soc2-prep-scratchpad-ava-patel
content:
SOC2 prep scratchpad - notes + questions (working)

Purpose: quick brain dump of outstanding questions and proposed control mappings for Trust Services Criteria. Will refine into control mapping doc and evidence checklist.

High-level scope
- Products in-scope: Hosted API, Dedicated (reserved), Private deployments (VPC/on-prem).
- Data in-scope: customer prompts, model outputs, user metadata (ids, billing info).
- Excluded: public model weights that are not customer-specific.

Primary TSC areas we need to cover (initial mapping thoughts)
- Security: access controls, network segmentation, encryption, MFA, IAM policies, admin ops
- Availability: capacity planning, autoscaling, DR runbooks
- Processing Integrity: input validation, model version pinning, rollback procedures
- Confidentiality: data-at-rest encryption, KMS integration, tenant separation (Dedicated vs Hosted)
- Privacy: data retention policies, deletion APIs, privacy notices

Open questions / risks (need answers from infra/product owners)
1) Key management: who rotates customer KMS keys for Private deploys? Is rotation automated or manual? (ask Solutions Eng + Infra)
2) Hosted API: do we persist raw prompts for debugging? retention period? link to hosted-api logging PR? (JIRA-SOC2-87)
3) Dedicated pools: are logs aggregated into central logging with customer identifiers? retention and access controls?
4) Incident response: do we have a tabletop/playbook specific to model-exfil/poisoning? Who declares breach threshold when model output reveals PII?
5) Private/on-prem: can customers provide their own evidence for physical security? what's the minimum evidence we accept?
6) Access reviews: cadence and owner for quarterly access review of privileged accounts (SRE, infra-admin).
7) Third-party vendors: which OSS libs could impact confidentiality (onnx, triton)? need third-party inventory ownership.

Quick control mapping draft (textual, to be converted to spreadsheet):
- CC: Access control (logical) -> Controls: IAM roles + RBAC, SSO + SCIM, MFA enforcement for admins. Evidence: SCIM provisioning logs, IdP attestations, monthly access review exports. Owner: infra -> tag: access-review
- CC: Logging & monitoring -> Controls: centralized ELK with RBAC, 90-day retention for security logs, alerting on anomalous burst traffic. Evidence: logging config, retention policy, sample alerts. Owner: observability
- CC: Encryption -> Controls: encryption-at-rest for data stores (S3 with SSE-KMS), TLS in transit always, KMS CMK rotation every 12 months. Evidence: KMS key policy, S3 encryption config. Owner: infra/security
- CC: Change management -> Controls: PR review policy, CI gating, deployment runbook, rollback tests. Evidence: PR checklist, deployment runbook, release notes. Owner: release-engineering
- CC: Vendor mgmt -> Controls: vendor inventory, risk assessment for critical libs, contract review for subproc. Evidence: vendor list, assessment doc. Owner: security-and-compliance

Evidence collection TODOs (short-term)
- Pull latest IdP provisioning report (Maya)
- Export access review CSV for privileged groups (infra-admins) - due: 2024-11-08 (Oliver)
- Confirm logging retention for Hosted API logs and Dedicated metrics (observability team)
- Draft incident response tabletop focused on model data leakage (assign to SRE + Applied ML)
- Create confluence page for private deployment evidence checklist (owner: me)

Notes to self / reminders
- Keep mapping flexible to accept customer-provided evidence for Private deployments; mark exact required items per deployment type (hosted vs dedicated vs private)
- Some controls will be shared responsibility (e.g., physical security for on-prem). Document boundary clearly.
- Need to capture demo evidence for rolling back model variants (show a canary rollback test and logs)

Small brainstorm: possible controls specific to inference platform
- KV cache isolation between tenants (verify cache keys include tenant-id)
- Model artifact signing and integrity checks during deployment
- Rate-limiting anomaly detection (for exfil attempts)
- Prompt redaction pipeline for long-term storage (strip PII before retention)

Meeting notes (from quick sync 2024-10-25)
- Infra to provide access review exports by 2024-11-08
- Observability to document log retention and storage location for customer data
- Product to list all endpoints that might store customer inputs/outputs
- Action: split evidence collection into Hosted/Dedicated/Private workstreams

Unresolved policy wording (draft snippets)
- "Retention of customer-provided prompts will not exceed 90 days in Hosted API unless explicitly opted-in for debugging by the customer." -> need legal sign-off
- "Private deployments: Redwood will provide control mapping and recommended evidence; customer is responsible for physical and local network controls unless contracted otherwise." -> confirm with Sales/Legal

Next steps (this week)
- Turn control mapping into spreadsheet with columns: control_id, description, TSC, evidence_list, owner, status
- Start filling evidence for top 10 highest-risk controls
- Schedule tabletop for incident response (model leak) - invite: SRE, Applied ML, Product Security

Links / refs
- Confluence: CONFLUENCE-1234 (SOC2 control catalog draft)
- Jira: JIRA-SOC2-87 (logging retention work)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/infra-pr-452 (encryption config changes)

Random adhoc thoughts
- Might be useful to include a sample customer questionnaire for Dedicated customers: do you need retained prompts? backup snapshots? encryption keys? (this will speed evidence collection)
- Consider automated evidence harvesters (scripts to dump access review CSVs, KMS policy snapshots) to reduce manual work

-- end of scratchpad --
